input: The central result of the pilot campaign was the capture of 82% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas, achieved during a 90-day campaign in which an amine absorption unit treated gas from a cement kiln at 15 t of carbon dioxide per day. Gas from the kiln was passed through the solvent in the absorber, and the capture figure represents the share of the carbon dioxide entering with that gas which the solvent took up, taken over the campaign as a whole. A campaign of this length carries the unit well past start-up behaviour: the solvent has been regenerated many times, the inventories have settled, and the figures describe sustained operation rather than the first days on a fresh charge. The steam demand was 3.9 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured. Since steam regenerates the solvent, the demand is effectively the energy cost of capture stated per tonne, and it is the figure from which an operating-cost estimate for any larger unit would be built. Solvent loss was 1.7 kg per tonne captured, a makeup cost that runs for as long as the unit runs and grows with the tonnage treated. It is important to appreciate that the two consumption figures and the capture figure belong together. A capture rate quoted without its steam demand states what the unit did but omits what the doing cost; a steam demand quoted without the capture rate has the same defect from the other side, because the demand is only meaningful against the tonnage it served. Read jointly, the campaign gives a complete operating picture at pilot scale: the rate of capture, the energy taken to sustain it, and the solvent consumed in sustaining it. Nevertheless, the campaign fixes every figure at 90 days. Beyond 90 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent remains untested. Dust reaches the solvent with the kiln gas throughout a campaign, and whether its effect accumulates as the campaign lengthens, or reaches a steady level and stops growing, is a question the present run cannot answer. Capture, steam demand and solvent loss beyond that point are not established, and any extension of the campaign would be a new test, not a continuation of this one's evidence.
